ideas.name: long_stroke_prismatic
ideas.description: A prismatic moving jaw on two 3 x 150 mm ground rods with LM3UU bushings. A 90-tooth module-0.5 pinion (pitch radius 22.5 mm, 46 mm across) on the servo horn drives a printed rack carriage, giving 22.5 mm of travel per rad. Over 1.9 rad that is about 43 mm of travel plus the fixed offset, for fingertips up to about 100 mm apart, with squeeze about 1.62/0.0225 = 72 N stall (about 35 N usable). The finger face stays vertical and the tip height constant at every opening.
ideas.test: Add a prismatic jaw variant to the simulator with a pinion pitch radius up to 22.5 mm and a carriage travel limit of 50 mm (rods 150 mm). Re-run all 21 objects, especially the dice (17 mm, at the low end of travel) and the 85-96 mm boxes.

ideas.name: self_aligning_pivot_pad
ideas.description: Each jaw gets a printed pad hung on a horizontal pivot at the stock fingertip: an M3 screw running through an MR63 bearing. The pad swings freely by about ±35 deg and is re-centred by a printed TPU flexure. It hangs 15-20 mm below the fingertip and has a 1 mm TPU face. On contact the pad turns until its face lies flat against the object's side, so the contact is antipodal at every opening instead of at the one opening a fixed pad_angle sets. The 15-20 mm drop also puts the contact below the box tops, even though the moving fingertip rises +15 to +17 mm at 76-78 mm. Narrow objects meet a pad that is already near parallel and self-centred, so banana and potted meat no longer set a cap on the tilt.
ideas.test: The simulator needs a pads variant with a passive hinge joint at the fingertip: a range limit of ±35 deg, a torsional spring of about 0.02 N*m/rad standing in for the TPU flexure, and a pad length (reach) of 15-20 mm. Run it on pudding_box, sugar_box, tuna_fish_can and gelatin_box, plus the held banana and potted_meat_can.

ideas.name: convex_barrel_pad
ideas.description: A printed PLA pad whose contact face is a convex cylinder of radius about 22 mm, with its axis parallel to the hinge axis, plus a 1 mm TPU skin and the same V-groove cut along the arc. It mounts with the existing two M2 screws per pad, at the current 30 deg base tilt. Because the face is curved, a horizontal-normal contact point exists for jaw tilts up to about ±40 deg. At wide openings that point sits low on the pad, so the moving jaw grips the box side instead of riding over its top corner. The fixed pad can stay flat, or take the same shape for symmetry.
ideas.test: Add a face_radius_mm parameter (0 = flat, 10-40 mm) to the pads part in design/fingers.py. It replaces the planar face with a cylindrical arc tangent to the current face at its midpoint, keeps the groove along the arc, and builds the collision mesh to match. Then run System 1 on every held group plus pudding_box, sugar_box and tuna_fish_can.

ideas.name: rise_compensating_cam_pad
ideas.description: The moving pad (today's 30 deg, 1 mm TPU, 24 mm wide, 0.6 mm groove) is printed on a carrier that slides vertically, with up to 20 mm of travel, in a printed dovetail on the moving jaw. An MR63 bearing on an M3 axle in the carrier runs in a closed cam slot cut in a plate screwed to the fixed gripper body, concentric with the jaw hinge. The slot runs at constant radius (no drop) up to a jaw angle of 0.86 rad, then its radius grows by 81(1 - cos q) - 81(1 - cos 0.86). As the jaw opens past 75 mm the pad is driven down by exactly the hinge's rise, so the moving tip stays level with the fixed tip at 85-95 mm. Because the slot is closed, the cam pushes the pad both ways: it cannot ride up when it meets a top edge, and no spring is needed.
ideas.test: The simulator needs a slide joint between the moving jaw and the pad, with its position tied to the jaw angle by the cam profile: equality-coupled, drop(q) = max(0, 81(cos 0.86 - cos q)) mm. Then rerun pudding, sugar and tuna at 85-92 mm, plus all held groups, to confirm nothing changes below 75 mm.

ideas.name: table_referenced_drop_pad
ideas.description: The moving pad is mounted on a carriage that slides vertically along the moving jaw on two 3 mm steel rods (cut to about 40 mm) in two LM3UU bushings, with 20 mm of travel and a printed hard stop at the bottom. The pad keeps the current design: 30 deg tilt, 1 mm TPU, 0.596 mm groove, 24 mm wide. The carriage hangs under its own weight (about 12 g with no spring), so when the hand comes down its foot settles onto the table and the face's lower edge always starts a few mm above the table, whatever the jaw angle. At wide openings the hinge has lifted the jaw by 14 to 22 mm, so the carriage hangs at its stop and the face closes on the box side below its top edge. At narrow openings the table pushes the carriage up into the jaw. Under load the object's weight goes into the bottom stop. The fixed pad is not changed. Added wrist mass is about 15 g.
ideas.test: The simulator needs a pads variant with a prismatic DOF on the moving pad: vertical slide along the jaw, 0 to 20 mm travel, gravity-loaded, a hard stop at the bottom, a table collision on the carriage foot and about 12 g carriage mass. Then run pudding_box, sugar_box and tuna_fish_can at 85 to 92 mm, and re-run banana, potted_meat_can, dice and large_marker to check the held groups.

ideas.name: long_radius_fingers
ideas.description:
Printed bolt-on extensions that lengthen both jaw fingers by 60 mm along their axes. The moving one goes on the stock hinged jaw, so its fingertip radius becomes about 141 mm instead of 81 mm. The fixed one is a straight vertical bar on the fixed jaw, keeping its face a vertical plane and level with the moving tip at closure. The existing pads (TPU skin, groove, 24 mm wide) mount on the new tips, with pad_angle re-tuned to about 18 to 20 deg.

Because the hinge sits farther above the contact, a given opening needs about half the jaw angle (about 0.54 rad instead of 1.1 at 90 mm). The tip rises about R(1-cos q) ≈ 40% less and the face swings about 40% less across 17 to 96 mm. The moving pad reaches the side of the 34 to 45 mm tall boxes instead of their tops. The cost is squeeze: torque/R, about 11.5 N instead of 20 N. Extension length is the design parameter: about 40 to 80 mm trades rise against squeeze.
ideas.test: A finger-length parameter on the jaw slot: the revolute jaw's hinge-to-fingertip radius (81 mm stock, range 81 to 161), plus a matching vertical extension of the fixed finger. Squeeze computed as servo torque over the new radius, and the extra finger mass (about 20 g) added at the wrist. Re-run System 1 on all 21 groups, with pad_angle free in 10 to 30 deg.

ideas.name: recentred_swing_fixed_jaw
ideas.description:
A replacement fixed jaw (the static half of the gripper, printed in PLA) whose contact face sits 39 mm farther from the moving jaw's hinge than the stock face. The moving fingertip then passes directly below its hinge, the lowest point of its 81 mm-radius arc, at a 45 mm opening instead of about 6 mm.

The moving jaw stays the stock part. Only its travel shifts: with the old fixed face gone it can swing about 0.6 rad past straight-down. The servo's 360 deg range covers this, so it needs a new lower joint limit in calibration, not a reprint. The working range becomes about -0.52 rad (5 mm opening) to +0.77 rad (about 101 mm).

The pads are reprinted at about a 5 deg tilt so the faces are parallel near 52 mm. Width, TPU and groove stay as now.

The new fixed finger is a stiff bracket (about a 10 x 15 mm section) carrying the 20 N squeeze about 80 mm down to the pad.
ideas.test: Add a jaw-slot builder 'revolute_recentred'. It should move the fixed face outward by fixed_offset_mm (range 0-45; 0 is today's jaw) and set the moving jaw's lower limit from where it hits the new fixed jaw. Then sweep fixed_offset_mm from 25 to 45 with pad_angle_deg from 0 to 15. Check the moving-tip height vs the fixed tip at 17, 57, 70, 85 and 92 mm, and run all 21 groups.

ideas.name: tendon_deployed_drop_tip
ideas.description: The lower 15 mm of the moving pad (keeping the 30 deg tilt, 1 mm TPU skin and 0.596 mm groove) is split off onto a printed PLA carriage. The carriage rides a 20 mm vertical dovetail on the moving jaw. A 2 mm x 1 mm TPU strap tied to the carriage runs over a printed post on the jaw and anchors on the fixed-jaw body. The strap's length makes it go taut at 75 mm of fingertip opening (about 0.86 rad). Past that, opening the jaw pulls the carriage down, about 12-15 mm by 92 mm, so the moving tip stays within about +13 mm of the fixed tip. A printed leaf spring lifts the carriage back against its top stop as the jaw closes below 75 mm, and the squeeze passes through the dovetail. Two M2 screws clamp the strap ends and two fix the dovetail.
ideas.test: A simulator builder for a two-body moving pad: a prismatic joint along the jaw's vertical axis with upper and lower limits, a tendon (spatial tendon with a slack length) from the carriage to a site on the fixed jaw, and a spring returning the carriage to its top stop. Then rerun all 21 groups, checking that the carriage stays on its top stop below 75 mm (apple, banana, gelatin, tomato, tennis unchanged).

proposals.mechanism: moving_jaw_on_top_face (pudding, sugar, mustard; fixed_jaw_missed on the tuna can likely the same geometry) and squeezed_down_out (gelatin): on the hinged jaw the moving fingertip rises +12..+26 mm above the fixed one and its face tilts 31-85 deg at the 70-80 mm closures, so it lands on or above the top edge of 30-58 mm tall boxes and pushes down at angles bare PLA (friction 0.45, about a 24 deg friction cone) cannot resist.
proposals.principle: A face that turns with its joint is parallel at one opening only. Tilting the moving pad back by 45 deg puts its parallel opening in the wide range (brief: 85 mm goes from face +53 deg, tip +23 mm to face +14 deg, tip +14 mm; 55 mm goes to -8 deg, -5 mm). A tilted contact holds while tan(a) < mu, and the TPU skin raises mu to 0.9 (about 42 deg), so every opening from 17 to 95 mm sits inside the cone. Extra reach lets the fingertips go deeper than the current fixed-contact height (about +0..3 mm on ~15-19 mm half-heights), so the remaining rise ends below the box top.
proposals.hypothesis: With the tip rise cut by about 9-10 mm at 73-92 mm and the faces within about 20 deg of parallel on high-friction TPU, both jaws reach the box sides: gelatin (top +15, tip ~+7), pudding (top +19, tip ~+16), sugar (top +23, tip ~+17), tuna (top +17, tip ~+14), and the mustard neck. No params move can do this because the stock hinge's tilt is fixed by geometry. Prismatic tops out at 68 mm, parallelogram rises even more (+33 mm at 85 mm), and 12 V servos are over budget and do not address geometry. 18 mm wide pads resist yaw on the long boxes and bottle. Cost: $0, 16 machine min, parts on hand (m2_screw x4, PLA 2 g, TPU 1 g).
risks: dice, large_marker, wood_block_cube, flat_screwdriver: at 17-35 mm the moving face now tilts the other way (about -21 to -32 deg) and its tip sits 10-12 mm below the fixed tip, so System 1 has to raise the hand to clear the table. It should survive: tan 32 deg = 0.62 < 0.9 with TPU, and the fixed jaw's vertical face still covers the object's side
golf_ball, plum, strawberry, lemon, racquetball: round objects now meet a face tilted about -8 to -15 deg below the equator, which pushes them up. The TPU friction cone should hold them
potted_meat_can (370 g, 0.35 friction): TPU friction more than doubles its friction margin; reach adds about 10% lever, so squeeze falls about 2 N

idea.name: long_stroke_prismatic
idea.description: A prismatic moving jaw on two 3 x 150 mm ground rods with LM3UU bushings. A 90-tooth module-0.5 pinion (pitch radius 22.5 mm, 46 mm across) on the servo horn drives a printed rack carriage, giving 22.5 mm of travel per rad. Over 1.9 rad that is about 43 mm of travel plus the fixed offset, for fingertips up to about 100 mm apart, with squeeze about 1.62/0.0225 = 72 N stall (about 35 N usable). The finger face stays vertical and the tip height constant at every opening.
idea.test: Add a prismatic jaw variant to the simulator with a pinion pitch radius up to 22.5 mm and a carriage travel limit of 50 mm (rods 150 mm). Re-run all 21 objects, especially the dice (17 mm, at the low end of travel) and the 85-96 mm boxes.

proposals.edit: pads -> pads (groove_mm=0, lip_mm=0, pad_angle_deg=30, pad_tpu_mm=3, reach_mm=6, width_mm=14)
proposals.mechanism: Wide boxes (gelatin box 73 mm, pudding box 90, sugar box 92, tuna can 85, mustard bottle 96): the moving jaw lands on the top face or squeezes the box down and out. On the stock hinge the fingertip has risen +12 to +17 mm at those openings, against box tops at +15 to +23 mm, and the moving face is 44-64 deg off parallel. The contacts read 52-85 deg pushing down. b000 (pad angle 45, reach 12) fixed this but lost apple, banana and potted_meat_can to force_limit (squeezing or pressing down). Those three sit at 57-75 mm, which is exactly where a 45 deg pad turns the face the other way (-8 deg at 55 mm, -21 deg at 35 mm) and drops the moving tip 5-10 mm below the fixed one.
proposals.principle: A face that turns with its joint is parallel at one opening only. A 45 deg back-tilt puts that opening near 85 mm, so every mid-width object is gripped by a reversed wedge (bottom swung in, tip low). With TPU friction 0.9 the wedge jams instead of slipping, and the servo keeps closing until a contact goes over the force limit. Setting pad_angle near 30 deg puts the parallel opening at about 57 mm, the width of the held potted-meat can and cup. From there the face tilt grows in the safe direction only: an estimated ~+14 deg at 75 mm, ~+23 at 85 and ~+30 at 92. All of these are below atan(0.9) = 42 deg, so the TPU friction still holds the tilted contacts.
proposals.hypothesis: An intermediate pad tilt keeps most of b000's gain on the wide boxes and removes the reversed wedge that overloaded the mid-width held objects. Params moves on the bare stock jaw cannot work: the stock face is 44-64 deg off parallel with its tip up +14 to +35 mm at 75-95 mm, at any servo angle. b000's tuning trials only nudged width, TPU and reach around angle 45, so the angle itself was never refit. Reach drops to 6 mm because the iteration-1 proposal with angle 38 and reach 20 was refused for pad-to-pad interference near closed. A shorter pad also cuts the extra tip rise that reach adds (pad angle 0 at 85 mm gives tip +27 vs stock +23). Cost is $0, 16 machine min, all on hand (m2 screws, 2 g PLA, 1 g TPU).
risks: potted_meat_can: 370 g of metal at friction 0.35. With the face near parallel at 57 mm it should be a plain antipodal grip. TPU 0.9 on the jaw side gives a friction limit of about 2*0.9*20 N, plenty of margin over 3.6 N.

apple / tomato_soup_can (75 / 68 mm, round): the face sits about +10-14 deg there, which pushes slightly down at the equator. TPU friction should hold it, as the stock jaw already does at +40 deg on PLA.
dice / large_marker / wood_block (17-26 mm): the face will be tilted about -20 deg, bottom in, which is less reversed than b000's 45 deg setting, and b000 kept these. The risk is low.

A shallow 2 mm V-groove centres round held objects (apple, tomato can) so they sit at the equator instead of riding the pad's edge.

It removes the low, protruding pad tip that I suspect overloaded apple, banana and the potted-meat can. This explores a different corner from b000's tuning, which held reach at 11.5-12.5 mm. Interference near closed should be well clear, since the refused case had reach 20.

sugar_box (514 g, 92 mm): with a short pad the tip may still rise to about +17 mm against its +23 top, which should be enough. The arm's shoulder load is 0.41 + 0.77 = 1.18 N*m, below the 1.62 N*m stall.

At those openings the stock moving jaw is 44-64 deg off parallel and its fingertip has risen +12 to +17 mm, while the box tops are at +15 to +23 mm. With TPU friction 0.9, the object wedges and the servo keeps closing until a contact overloads. A 30 deg tilt makes the face parallel near 57 mm and keeps it under the 42 deg TPU friction limit out to 92 mm.

**Proposal 2 (pad tilt 40 deg, reach 3 mm, 2 mm groove):** this tests the other explanation, that the 12 mm pad extension is what pushes the low tip into the object. The groove centres the round held objects.

- **The slide jaw** opens only 68 mm, which loses apple and the tomato soup can.
- **The four-bar jaw** at 90 mm links keeps the face parallel, but its fingertip rises +33 mm at 85 mm, worse than stock.
- **The 12 V servos** were refused because they cost $68 against the $40 left.

The mustard bottle (96 mm wide, 58 tall) is likely to stay failing under both proposals.

iterations.notes:
I've proposed two pad-parameter changes for this round, both at no cost. They depend on one guess: that the TPU skin is what broke apple, banana and the potted-meat can. The simulator hasn't tested that yet.

**What the trials show so far.** The 45° pad (b000) fixed all four box/can failures. It brought the moving fingertip down below the box tops and made the jaw faces close to parallel. It also lost apple, banana and the potted-meat can, all by going over the force limit, mostly right at first contact (t = 0.02 s). Every pad trial so far used a 2.8–3 mm TPU skin, so we've never seen the pads without it.

**My guess.** The fingertip swings on an arc as it closes, so it slides up or down the object's side. On bare PLA (friction 0.45) it slips. On TPU (friction 0.9) it can grip and drag the object into the table, which would produce exactly these early force spikes. We don't need TPU for weight. The heaviest object is the 514 g sugar box (about 5 N). Bare PLA at 20 N squeeze gives 2 × 0.45 × 20 = 18 N of grip, and it already holds the 370 g metal potted-meat can today.

**The two proposals:**
1. **b000 with the TPU removed** (45° tilt, 12 mm reach). I expect gelatin box, pudding box, sugar box and tuna can to start passing.
2. **b011 with the TPU removed** (40° tilt, 3 mm reach, 2 mm groove). I expect gelatin box and tuna can to pass without losing banana.

Running both also separates the causes. If both keep banana, friction was the cause. If only the second does, the 12 mm reach was. The risk is that the losses come from the pad shape rather than friction, in which case they stay lost. The loop's four tuning trials can then adjust reach and angle.

**Why no other part:**
- **Hinged parallel-jaw linkage:** at 85 mm its fingertip sits 33 mm up, above the box tops.
- **Sliding jaw:** it opens to at most 68 mm, too narrow for these boxes.
- **12 V servos:** they cost $68 and $40 is left.
- **Stock jaw with new settings:** its fingertip sits 14–23 mm up at 75–85 mm, whatever the servo angle.

**Mustard bottle (96 mm) is not addressed.** The pads open to at most 95 mm, and no part we can afford in the catalogue fits it. The long-stroke slide idea recorded in iteration 1 is still the only path for it.

Both proposals need only 4 M2 screws (on hand) and a few grams of PLA, about 16 machine-minutes each, with no TPU and nothing to buy.

idea.name: self_aligning_pivot_pad
idea.description: Each jaw gets a printed pad hung on a horizontal pivot at the stock fingertip: an M3 screw running through an MR63 bearing. The pad swings freely by about ±35 deg and is re-centred by a printed TPU flexure. It hangs 15-20 mm below the fingertip and has a 1 mm TPU face. On contact the pad turns until its face lies flat against the object's side, so the contact is antipodal at every opening instead of at the one opening a fixed pad_angle sets. The 15-20 mm drop also puts the contact below the box tops, even though the moving fingertip rises +15 to +17 mm at 76-78 mm. Narrow objects meet a pad that is already near parallel and self-centred, so banana and potted meat no longer set a cap on the tilt.
idea.test: The simulator needs a pads variant with a passive hinge joint at the fingertip: a range limit of ±35 deg, a torsional spring of about 0.02 N*m/rad standing in for the TPU flexure, and a pad length (reach) of 15-20 mm. Run it on pudding_box, sugar_box, tuna_fish_can and gelatin_box, plus the held banana and potted_meat_can.

I've sent two proposals. Neither adds a group for sure, and four groups still fail.

**What's failing.** All four (pudding box, sugar box, mustard bottle, tuna can) fail the same way: the moving jaw lands on the object's top face instead of its side. On the stock hinged jaw, the moving fingertip rises above the fixed one as the jaw opens: +22 mm at 85 mm, +34 mm at 95 mm. Its face also leans in at the top, by 28-39 deg. So the upper part of the pad hits the box's top corner first and pushes down.

**Why parts from the list don't fix it.**
- **Parallelogram jaw:** its fingertip rises even more, +46 mm at 85 mm.
- **Slide jaw:** it neither rises nor tilts, but it opens only to 60 mm. That would drop apple, banana, gelatin box, tennis ball and soup can.
- **12 V servos:** can't be bought ($68 needed, $40 left), and arm strength is not the problem here anyway.
- **Pad tilt:** six iterations of record show the trade-off. Any tilt from 33 to 45 deg wins the wide boxes but loses banana or potted meat. 30 deg keeps both but wins only gelatin box.

**Proposal 1: tilt the pads 31.5 deg ($0, about 9 machine min).** Every other pad value stays exactly as now. The tuna can was won at 33 deg, banana is held at 30 deg, and nothing in between has been tried. This tests whether the tuna can switches to passing before banana switches to failing. Banana is a real risk, and the trial decides.

**Proposal 2: a new part, a curved pad face (recorded, not tested).** It needs only print time plus four M2 screws already on hand. A pad face curved like a barrel always has some point facing the box side straight on, so it grips flat with the fixed jaw at every opening. At wide openings that point sits lower on the pad, which also helps against the rising fingertip. No pad setting in the list makes the face curved; the groove setting is concave and the lip is a hook. Testing it needs a curve-radius setting added to `design/fingers.py`. Potted meat is its risk: a curved face touches along a line, which resists twisting less than a flat face.

**Mustard bottle: no single pad change will win it.** It is 96 mm across, and the current jaw with pads opens to at most 95 mm. Bare jaw faces open to 99 mm, but that drops pad friction from 0.9 to 0.45, which risks the heavy, slippery metal cans. Winning it needs bare faces, a thinner pad or the longer slide jaw already recorded as an idea. That idea needs 150 mm rods, which the bench doesn't stock; I estimated them at $4.

idea.name: rise_compensating_cam_pad
idea.description: The moving pad (today's 30 deg, 1 mm TPU, 24 mm wide, 0.6 mm groove) is printed on a carrier that slides vertically, with up to 20 mm of travel, in a printed dovetail on the moving jaw. An MR63 bearing on an M3 axle in the carrier runs in a closed cam slot cut in a plate screwed to the fixed gripper body, concentric with the jaw hinge. The slot runs at constant radius (no drop) up to a jaw angle of 0.86 rad, then its radius grows by 81(1 - cos q) - 81(1 - cos 0.86). As the jaw opens past 75 mm the pad is driven down by exactly the hinge's rise, so the moving tip stays level with the fixed tip at 85-95 mm. Because the slot is closed, the cam pushes the pad both ways: it cannot ride up when it meets a top edge, and no spring is needed.
idea.test: The simulator needs a slide joint between the moving jaw and the pad, with its position tied to the jaw angle by the cam profile: equality-coupled, drop(q) = max(0, 81(cos 0.86 - cos q)) mm. Then rerun pudding, sugar and tuna at 85-92 mm, plus all held groups, to confirm nothing changes below 75 mm.

- **Pad tilt:** tilts above 30 deg have lost the banana every time, even at 31.5 deg.
- **Prismatic jaw:** it opens at most 60 mm, so it would lose every held object wider than that.
- **Parallelogram jaw:** its tip rises even more (+46 mm at 85 mm).

**Proposal 2 (idea): a cam-driven drop pad.**
- **How it works:** the pad rides a short vertical slide on the moving jaw. A slot cut in a plate on the fixed body steers it, so the pad drops by exactly the hinge's rise, but only past 75 mm.
- **Why only past 75 mm:** below that, the 17 held groups see today's geometry unchanged.
- **Cost:** one MR63 bearing ($0.90, 3 days) plus screws on hand, 7 g PLA and 1 g TPU, about 43 machine minutes.
- **Difference from earlier ideas:** it corrects tip height at wide openings only. The recorded pivot and barrel pads change face angle and contact position instead.

**Expected gains.** Pudding box, sugar box and tuna can. Tuna is the weakest of the three: it is metal with low friction, and the face would still be about 28 deg off parallel. I'm not claiming mustard: at 96 mm it's wider than the jaw's 95 mm maximum opening, so nothing in this slot can reach it.

proposals.mechanism: moving_jaw_on_top_face. On all 8 failing tasks the hinged moving fingertip is 11 to 22 mm above the fixed one when it makes contact, and the box tops sit at +17 to +29 from the centre. The moving pad lands on the top edge and pushes 71 to 85 deg down, the fixed jaw often never touches, and nothing rises more than 2 mm. In the brief, the tip rises +13 at 75 mm, +22 at 85 mm and +34 at 95 mm because it swings on an 81 mm radius through about 1.0 to 1.1 rad.
proposals.principle: A fingertip on a swinging joint rises by about R(1-cos q), and the opening grows by about R·Δsin q. For a given opening the rise therefore scales roughly as w²/2R, and the face's angle swing scales as w/R. Raising the hinge relative to the contact (a longer R) cuts both: less rise at wide openings and a narrower spread of face angles over the whole object range. Squeeze falls as torque/R.
proposals.hypothesis:
The catalogue is exhausted for this mechanism, and the record shows it.
- Pad tilt is the only pads parameter that lowers the wide-opening tip. It gains pudding, sugar and tuna at 33 to 40 deg, but every tilt above 30 deg lost banana (5 bodies, including 31.5 deg).
- Pad reach extends along the tilted pad, so at 85 mm (face 28 deg bottom-out) it lowers the moving tip less than the fixed one. Reach 12 gained nothing and lost apple and potted meat.
- The parallelogram rises more (+46 mm at 85 mm, link 90).
- The prismatic jaw opens at most 60 mm.
- 12 V servos are refused on budget ($68 vs $40) and don't address the mechanism anyway.

The idea: lengthen both fingers by 60 mm along the jaw line, so the hinge sits about 141 mm above the contact instead of 81 mm. The fixed finger keeps its vertical face; the current 30 deg TPU pads move to the new tips.

Estimate, scaled from the brief's numbers (a 25 mm rise from 17 to 85 mm on R=81, against about 37 mm of raw R(1-cos q)): 90 mm now needs about q≈0.54 rad instead of about 1.1. The moving tip should then sit about +10 to +13 mm at 90 mm (pudding top +19), +11 to +14 at 92 mm (sugar top +23) and +8 to +10 at 85 mm (tuna top +17). That puts it on the side face, below each top.

The face spread over 17 to 96 mm drops from about 61 deg (-22 to +39) to about 35 deg. Pad angle can then be re-tuned to about 18 to 20 deg, which helps antipodality everywhere, without the extra tilt that keeps losing banana.

Squeeze falls from 20 N to about 1.62/0.141 ≈ 11.5 N, still above weight with margin:
- sugar 514 g: 2·0.5·11.5 = 11.5 N vs 5.0 N
- potted meat 370 g: 2·0.35·11.5 = 8 N vs 3.6 N
- mustard 431 g: 9.2 N vs 4.2 N

mustard_bottle may still fail: its equator needs the tip near 0 mm, and about +13 to +16 is estimated.

idea.name: long_radius_fingers
idea.description:
